1. Complex medial meniscal tear: This refers to a tear in the meniscus, which is a cartilage structure that provides cushioning and stability to the knee joint. A complex tear implies that the tear extends into multiple areas or is of a more severe nature.

2. Subchondral fracture of the medial tibial plateau: This means there is a fracture in the bone just below the cartilage found on the inner part of the upper surface of the tibia (shinbone). 3. Severe patellofemoral chondral pathology: This indicates significant damage to the cartilage between the patella (kneecap) and the femur (thigh bone). This damage can result in pain, reduced range of motion, and decreased function of the knee joint.

4. Pes anserinus bursitis: Pes anserinus bursitis refers to inflammation of the pes anserinus bursa, a small fluid-filled sac located near the inner side of the knee. This condition is typically associated with overuse or injury and can cause pain and swelling in the knee.

5. Mucoid degeneration of ACL: Mucoid degeneration refers to the breakdown and abnormal thickening of the fibers within a structure. In this case, it is the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in the knee that is affected. This degeneration can weaken the ligament, leading to instability and increased risk of further injury.

A engenharia é, por sua natureza, uma disciplina quantitativa e o elemento-chave de qualquer processo de engenharia é a medição. Conforme Pressman e Maxim (2016, p. 653), a “métrica de produto ajuda os engenheiros de software a visualizar o projeto e a construção do software, focando nos atributos específicos e mensuráveis dos artefatos da engenharia de software”. Ela é usada para melhorar o entendimento dos atributos dos modelos criados e para avaliar a qualidade dos sistemas.

 

Por que medir os produtos? Para obter controle de um projeto e também para gerenciá-lo, além disso, a medição permite avaliar se estamos perto ou longe dos objetivos planejados. Um engenheiro de software coleta medidas e desenvolve métricas para obter indicadores.

 

De acordo com o texto supracitado responda qual das afirmações abaixo é verdadeira.

a.
A medição é fundamental para o controle e gerenciamento de projetos de software, permitindo avaliar se os objetivos planejados estão sendo atingidos.


b.
A medição não é importante na engenharia de software, pois a disciplina não é quantitativa.


c.
A medição é usada apenas para avaliar a qualidade dos sistemas e não tem relação com o controle e gerenciamento de projetos.


d.
A medição é importante apenas para coletar dados para relatórios, não tendo relação com o planejamento e execução do projeto.


e.
A medição é usada para definir objetivos planejados, mas não tem relação com o controle e gerenciamento do projeto de software.

So far this is my methodology chapter. I would like you to read and evaluate and whether my approach is good or not. Remember the language should be formal and scientifc
In this thesis, the two different architectural patterns were applied on two applications containing machine learning components respectively. The architectural patterns were Client-Server architecture and Micro-services architecture and the two applications containing ML components were an End-to-End Task-Completion (TC) Chatbot and an online learning application. *The goal was to investigate the effects of rearchitecting the application and applying these patterns on the applications by comparing the performance before and after applying the pattern and document any challenges encountered during implementation and any modifications to the architectural pattern* . The choice of the Client-Server pattern to be applied on the End-to-End Task-Completion Chatbot was because of the Client-Server being the second most used architectural pattern for software-only applications and it served as a good opportunity to investigate the adoption of a software architectural pattern to a Machine Learning application mostly consisting of machine learning modules and whether or not the same advantages of the pattern apply to the ML application. *The choice of applying micro-services pattern on the online learning application was due to the fact that the application containing both software and machine learning components that interact with each other.*

In this section, first, the author of the thesis will fully explain the modules of the first application. Next, he will discuss the current interactions between the modules and the flow of the application. Then, he will describe the current architecture of the application and derive. Then, he will describe the application after implementing the Client-Server architectural pattern. ****The author of the thesis used a publicly available simulation framework designed for the movie-booking domain as his first application. The framework is made of several components that make a practical dialogue system: “The natural language understanding (NLU) module”, “The natural language generation (NLG) module”, “Knowledge bases (KBs)”, “State Trackers”, “Agents” and “Dialog Manager”. The natural language understanding (NLU) module transforms natural-language  texts to structured semantic frames of utterances. The natural language generation (NLG) module converts the structured representations back into a natural-language form. Knowledge bases (KBs) provide access to information and state trackers keep track of the state of the dialogue and previous history. The Agent tries to accomplish the end-goal of the user by choosing an action given the state of the dialog and Dialog Manager orchestrates the dialogue between the user and the agent.  The framework have two types of agents which are a rule-based and reinforcement learning agent. Rule-based agents apply explicit rules to choose the action given the state of the dialogue while the reinforcement learning agent's choice of action is learnt from experience. Reinforcement learning (RL) methods were chosen instead of supervised learning (SL) to be used by the agent. This was because SL approaches often require a large amount of expert-labeled data for training which can be expensive and time-consuming for task-specific domains as intensive domain knowledge is needed for collecting and annotating actual human-human or human-machine conversations. *Additionally, even with a large amount of training data, it is possible that some dialogue state spaces may not be explored sufficiently in the training data, preventing a supervised learner to find a good policy. In contrast, RL approaches allow an agent to learn without any expert-generated example. Given only a reward signal, the agent can optimize a dialogue policy through interaction with users.* In this framework a user simulator is used to act as the user and simulator supports two tasks: movie ticket booking and movie seeking. A user simulator was chosen instead of a real user because RL require numerous samples which makes it impractical to learn from scratch with real users. The goal of the agent is to assist user simulator in booking movie tickets or searching for specific movies through natural language interaction. 

Throughout the conversation, the agent collects information about the user's preferences and ultimately proceeds to book the movie tickets or identify the desired movie. At the conclusion of the conversation, the system evaluates the outcome as either successful or unsuccessful based on two criteria: (1) whether a movie is successfully booked and (2) whether the movie meets the user's specified constraints. The data that was used was collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk. There are 11 intents (i.e., inform, request, confirm_question, confirm_answer, etc.), and 29 slots (i.e., movie name, start time, theater, number of people, etc.) and the slots are either informable slots, which user simulator tells the agent, or requestable slots, which users can ask values from the agent. Every time when a dialogue is run, a random user goal is chosen from the dataset and, to make the user goal more realistic, certain slots elements must appear in every user goal and these elements are “movie name”, “theater”, “start time”, “date”, “number of people”. 

The dialog manager initiates the dialog by calling the user simulator to take the first turn and choose a random goal. The user simulator requests the random goal to be fulfilled and this goal contains informable slots and request slots. This goal is converted to natural language using the NLG module and then the result natural language is  fed into the NLU module to imitate a real user inputing their goal in natural language. The result natural language is displayed by the dialog manager. This whole sequence of actions results in a 'user action'. The state tracker then processes the user action, extracts its inform slots and request slots to store them and keep track of the state of the dialog. The dialog manager module then calls the agent respond. The agent learns of the state of the dialog from the state tracker and chooses the appropriate 'agent action' based on its type. The agent action is converted into natural language by the NLG and displayed. The state tracker, with the help of the knowledge base, is updated with the recent agent action. The user simulator then evaluates the response from state tracker and replies accordingly. The described sequence between the agent and user is repeated until either the agent satisfies all the requirements of the user, which marks a successful dialog, or until a maximum number of turns is exceeded, which marks a failed dialog. Based on the outcome of the dialog, the user then chooses a reward. This is the simulation of one dialog. If the agent is a RL agent, the agent needs to be trained first. Warm start simulation is conducted before the training and rule policies are applied to populate the agent's experience replay pool, which represents minimum experience needed before agent can can leverage its RL methods to take decision.

 The agent is then trained M number of episodes, which represents a sequence of interactions between an agent and its the user, starting from an initial state and continuing until a terminal state is reached. with each episode containing M number of epochs (dialogs). At the end of every episode, the maximum between the success rate of the episode, which is the ratio between the number of successful epochs to the number of M epochs, and the best success rate obtained so far is chosen to keep track of the best model as well as the performance records.

The current architecture of the framework is shown in Figure 1. This architecture does not follow any any architectural pattern proposed in the literature review. The architecture is described as follows: 

- It consists of the seven previously discussed modules - 'Dialog Manager', 'User Simulator', 'Agent', 'NLG', 'NLU', 'State Tracker', 'Knowledge Base'.
- The dialog manager keeps an instance of all of the user simulator, agent and state tracker.
- The user simulator keeps an instance of NLG and NLU.
- The agent keeps an instance of NLG
- The state tracker keeps an instance of the knowledge base

In this architecture, the dialog manager updates the state tracker with the ‘user action’ and the ‘agent action’ and it prints the actions as it .The reason behind the user simulator having both NLU and NLG instances is, as mentioned previously, to simulate the action of a real user entering input in natural language format .The reason that the NLG component was shown twice in the figure is because the user simulator and agent keep different instances of the NLG. The instances of the modules are created in a run file that parses the input arguments and launches the simulation. The arguments are the predefined settings of the framework such as the type of the agent, the maximum number of turns, the number of episodes, the file path of the trained model and the experience replay pool size. These arguments are used by both the user simulator and the agent.
In Client-Server architectural pattern, the system is divided into two parts, one act as a client and other as a server. Hence to implement the architectural pattern, the application modules should be divided into two parts, a client-side and a server-side. According to Sharmaa et al [3] , the client is the requester of the service, while the server accepts the client's request, carries out the necessary processing, collects the required information, generates a solution to fulfill the client's demand, and subsequently sends the generated solution back to the client. Following the definition of the client and server, the author of the thesis proceeded to categorize the modules into either ‘Client-side’, ‘Server-side’, ‘Both’ or ‘Refactoring is required’. The ‘refactoring is required’ module means that the module, in its current state, could not be fit into the client-side or the server-side and, hence, modifications were required to fit either of them. The following is the categorization of the modules:

- User simulator: Client-side. The client is the requester of the service and in the context of the task completion framework, the user simulator requests the booking of movie tickets. The output of the user simulator is displayed on the server-side.
- Agent: Server-side. The server processes the request and accordingly generates a solution to the request.In the context of the framework, both Rule-Based agent and RL agent attempts to fulfill the movie booking request and, thus the whole agent module is considered as the server. The output of the agent is displayed on the server-side.
- NLU: Client-side. As shown in figure 1, the user simulator, which is on the client-side, has an instance of NLU, while the agent, which is on the server-side, does not have an instance of NLU and hence, NLU was chosen to be in the client-side
- NLG: Both. As shown in figure 1, the user simulator and the agent, which are on the client-side and server-side respectively, have two different instances of the NLG and so, the author of thesis opted to include the NLG on both modules. The NLG could also  have alternatively been implemented on the server-side only, however this adds unnecessary complexity since, as previously discussed, the ‘user action’ generated by the user simulator is transferred as input to the NLG module and its output is further processed by the NLU module to imitate a real user. Hence, to preserve the imitation of the real user sequence on the client-side, there must be a NLG module on the client-side. There must be a NLG module on the server-side as well because it is essential such that the mapping of the agent's response into natural language is performed and presented  to the user on the server-side.
- State tracker: Server-side. As previously mentioned, state tracker keep track of the state of the dialogue as well as the previous history and is updated by both ‘user action’ and ‘agent action’. Despite the state tracker being utilized by both modules, neither agent nor user simulator have an instance of the state tracker. The rationale for implementing the state tracker ***on***  the server side ***was***  that state tracker provides a service to the user simulator and it does not issue requests. Accordingly, the author of the thesis chose implement the state track on the server side to abide by the principle of the Client-Server architecture.
- Knowledge base: Server-side. Knowledge base is an instance of the state tracker which is on the server-side and it is needed to provide information to the state tracker. Hence, the knowledge base was implemented on the server-side.
- Dialog Manager: Refactoring is required. As shown in figure 1, the dialog manager keeps an instance of agent and state tracker, both of which are on the server-side, and the user simulator, which is on the client-side. Furthermore, as elaborated earlier, the dialog manager performs several functionalities to these modules such as calling the agent and user simulator to take their respective turns, print their actions and update the actions of the agent and the user simulator in the state tracker. To preserve the functionalities the dialog manager performs and at the same time apply the Client-Server architecture pattern, the dialog manager’s logic required to be refactored. The exact restructuring of the module is described by the author of the thesis below.

I*n order to align the dialog manager with the Client-Server architecture*, the author of the thesis inspected closely the current implementation of the dialog manager and its methods. The dialog manager has an instance of the user simulator, agent and state tracker. When the dialog manager is initialized, it initializes the three modules and calls the user to take the first turn. The dialog manager summons the agent to take its turn, updates the state tracker with the agent action, calls the user to reply to the agent and update the state tracker with this user action all in one method. Further more, the dialog manager prints the action of the agent and user in one method. Therefore, in order to align with the Client-Server architecture, the client related functionalities and the server related functionalities were  separated into two new modules: 'Dialog Manager Client' and ' Dialog Manager Server'

- Dialog Manager Client handles all the operations performed by the dialog manager for the client modules. These operations are initiating the user simulator module to select the goal to take the first turn, summoning the user simulator to reply in its respective turn and displaying the output of the user simulator. The Dialog Manager Client module is implemented on the Client-Side
- Dialog Manager Server handles all the operations performed by the dialog manager for the server modules. These operations are initiating the agent, summoning the agent to reply in its respective turn, updating the state tracker with the current state of the dialog and displaying the output of the agent. The Dialog Manager Server module is implemented on the Server-Side.

Abiding by his classification of the modules into client and server and by the Client-Server architectural pattern, the author of the thesis proposed the architecture shown in Figure 2. This architecture is divided into two parts, a client and a server and it consists of eight modules.

Все выявленные элементы необходимо представить в виде ценностной системы.
Ситуация «Культура Сбербанка»
Сбербанк, крупнейший банк страны, с приходом Германа Грефа начал меняться – новые и отремонтированные офисы с кондиционерами, системы электронной очереди и стулья для ожидающих клиентов, улыбки на лицах работников, готовых (иногда даже слишком навязчиво) оказать посетителю любую помощь.
Чтобы добиться этого, руководству Сбербанка пришлось менять своих сотрудников (около 250 тыс. человек) — и в прямом, и в переносном смысле. Изменения в Сбербанке начались в конце 2007—2008 гг. У реформирования банка не было экономических причин, это была исключительно политическая воля. Банк за эти годы изменился: поменялся логотип, сократилось название, а у сотрудников появилась «униформа». Началось внедрение модной на Западе системы lean-менеджмента — фактически сокращения избыточных расходов. Для оценки компетенции сотрудников придумали систему, которая называется «5+». Работника проверяли по ряду критериев, и в итоге составлялся портрет сотрудника: его относили к одной из категорий «плохой работник», «хороший работник», «звезда». Эта технология распространилась в 2010 г. на все отделения. Были внедрены ПСС — производственные системы Сбербанка. В основу концепции ПСС положена философия постоянного совершенствования и бережливого производства. Используя эту концепцию, стремились к качественным изменениям в трех направлениях: оптимизации процессов, улучшения системы управления и изменения менталитета и ценностей сотрудников.
Главное направление изменения менталитета сотрудников — установка на то, что клиент всегда прав.
Было принято, что на столе каждого работника должен быть только один карандаш, одна ручка, за опоздание на минуту — штраф. Определенного свода требований нет, есть общие принципы. В одном московском отделении на столе стоит телефон со стикером «телефон», степлер с надписью «степлер», ластик с надписью «ластик», так  как местный начальник обязал сотрудников подписать каждый предмет. От результатов выполнения ПСС зависит размер премий: при проверке каждому отделению присваивается определенное место в рейтинге. В компании часто проводят тимбилдинги, поют песни и гимны «Сбербанка», водят хороводы и т.д. Каждое утро сотрудникам приходят письма «Доброе утро, Сбербанк!» от Германа Грефа с какими-то советами или пожеланиями. Например, «если вам по телефону звонит начальник встаньте и поприветствуйте его стоя — это поднимет ваш боевой дух», работникам настоятельно рекомендуют читать определенные книги. Некоторые сотрудники сдавали нечто вроде зачетов по этим книгам. Книги по бизнесу и психологии были изданы «Альпина Паблишера» специальным тиражом: в начале каждой книги шло письмо Грефа примерно такого содержания: «Эти книги изменили мою жизнь и вашу, дорогие сотрудники, надеюсь, тоже изменят».
Весь корпоративный дух сегодня пронизан темой уважения к клиенту. И если сотрудник не разделяет эту ценность, то сотрудника могут попросить уволиться. Как и в любом банке, в Сбербанке находили людей, занимающихся сомнительными операциями с денежными средствами. Но только Сбербанк пошел на беспрецедентную в банковском сообществе открытость — в 2010г. он опубликовал на своем сайте списки сотрудников, «уволенных по инициативе работодателя». Речь шла о людях подозреваемых в недобросовестности при совершении финансовых операций, а также получивших неоднократные дисциплинарные взыскания. Таких набралось более 400 человек. Юристы говорили тогда, что фигуранты черного списка могут подать| па банк в суд и требовать компенсации за нанесение им морального вреда и ущерба репутации — и такой прецедент был, однако автор иска в итоге забрала его назад.
Вместо сокращенных сотрудников старой закалки в Сбербанк приходили новые, молодые. Зачастую прямо из банковского колледжа — после практики. Молодые сотрудники проходят много проверок.
В банке стремятся сократить очереди, расчет такой: чем меньше очередь, тем больше сотрудник может клиенту продать, это называется «кросс-продажи» — когда клиент приходит платить коммуналку, ему предлагают дополнительные услуги — банковские карты, оплату через Интернет и всякое такое, кредиты и пр. Очереди (в них всегда было много пенсионеров) необходимо было убрать, чтобы привлечь кредитоспособных клиентов из МВС — массового высокодоходного сегмента, т.е. людей, чьи доходы превышают 100 тыс. руб. в месяц. Если очередь большая, то такие люди уходят оплачивать счета в другие банки, соответственно, надо было эту очередь убрать, чтобы они могли нормально обслуживаться в Сбербанке. Рост кредитного портфеля банка пошел имени именно тогда, когда были проведены подобные преобразования.
И все же в первую очередь руководство пыталось добиться, чтобы сотрудники не хамили клиентам. Достаточно было трех замечаний в книге жалоб, и невежливого сотрудника увольняли. Первая жалоба — выговор сотруднику, вторая жалоба — выговор сотруднику и управляющему, третья — увольнение сотрудника и управляющего. Сотруднику чаще всего все равно, вроде как «будет выговор — уйду в другой банк», а управляющего этот момент стимулировал. Не нахамить клиенту — это полдела, надо еще быть с ним обходительным и улыбаться. Обычный клиент, конечно, не им пишет жалобу, если ему не улыбнуться, но за сотрудниками следят еще и в рамках маркетингового исследования «тайный покупатель» — этим занимаются в различным регионах разные фирмы, которые Сбербанк находит в ходе открытых конкурсов.
Новых сотрудников обучают на специальных тренингах. Например, на занятиях в учебном центре Среднерусского банка Сбербанка проводится игра «Довольный клиент». Сюжет деловой игры — клиент, владелец малого предприятия, пришел только за  кредитом для малого бизнеса, задача участников игры — убедить его воспользоваться дополнительными банковскими услугами, исходя из величины оборота, прибыли, количества сотрудников, сферы деятельности и т.п.
Все отделения Сбербанка должны работать в едином стиле, определять потребности клиентов. Тренинги проходят динамично, видно, что сберовцам обучение нравится. Ведь они материально заинтересованы в том, чтобы клиент «купил» как можно больше банковских услуг. За это им полагаются премии. Обучению в Сбербанке придается огромное значение — все его сотрудники так или иначе проходят различные курсы и тренинги и в начале работы в банке, и в процессе работы. В банке отработан целый ряд курсов и тренингов, которые будут объединены под названием «Корпоративный университет», начали внутрикорпоративную Executive MBA для сотрудников. Сбербанк готов обучать не только сотрудников: московское отделение Сбербанка открыло курсы для пенсионеров, где будут рассказывать о банковских продуктах, услугах Пенсионного фонда Росси и деятельности и возможностях общественных организаций. В банке обещают, что некоторые слушатели курсов в будущем смогут получить работу в Сбербанке. Будут консультировать своих сверстников.

翻译：Give the people what they want: putting these lessons into practice

With all this in mind, how can you apply these principles across your business? While there are a number of ways to implement these ideas, I’ve spent the bulk of my career helping teams leverage a marketing platform like HubSpot to architect and deliver remarkable customer experiences. A number of platforms on the market may also have at least some of these features, or a comparable alternative, but here’s how I’d recommend moving forward if you do use the HubSpot suite of tools, but the general lessons are applicable to other platforms too.  
Marketing: provide relevant content

In the B2B landscape, providing relevant content is key to engaging potential clients and nurturing existing relationships.

Leverage your marketing platform to:

    Sync ads audiences. This allows for targeted advertising, ensuring that the right content reaches the right audience. Use your CRM data to create highly targeted ad campaigns and uncover valuable insight.
    Create multiple blogs for various audiences. By having different blogs for different segments, you can tailor content to specific needs and interests.
    Use a newsletter builder. A tool like this helps to create customized newsletters, providing relevant information and updates to subscribers.
    Set specific segmentation and lead scoring. With precise targeting and prioritization of leads, you can ensure marketing efforts are directed where they’ll have the most impact.

Part of this mindset is about meeting customers on their own time, rather than interrupting them. Notice that only one of these four items is about ads: by being content-forward, you allow customers to take the next steps at their own pace, creating a more pleasant experience.

The key is to balance both strategies, using outbound methods to complement and enhance the inbound approach. Speaking of outbound…
Sales: ensure consistent customer experiences

Consistency in customer experiences is vital for building trust and facilitating smooth transactions. From clearly defining sales rep interactions to creating a consistent way to present quotes, you can leverage your software for more reliably positive experiences.

What can you do to improve sales experience consistency?

    Use something like HubSpot Playbooks for consistent data across reps. This ensures that all sales representatives have access to the same information, leading to uniform and consistent interactions.
    Use easy quoting and transacting mechanisms. Use these types of features to streamline the sales process, making it easier for customers to understand pricing and to complete transactions.
    Use a knowledge center to provide consistent answers. Sales reps should all be able to access a centralized knowledge base so customers aren’t given conflicting information or accidental false promises.

If you use HubSpot, be sure to take advantage of the detailed segmentation capabilities in your account so you can more easily customize leads’ experiences, and ensure that sales interactions are tailored to their individual needs.
Email personalization: use data points to make emails more personal

Personalized emails resonate more with recipients, leading to higher engagement rates. That’s more than just a simple “Dear [NAME]”. In fact, the fake personalization (as we call that) is often more of a damaging behavior, especially if any of those fields are wrong. 

The moral of the story here is sending emails that are relevant to the customer based on their interests or behavior. Use the right tools to customize your emails:

    Contact properties. This allows for detailed profiling of contacts, enabling highly personalized email content.
    Segmentation, lifecycle stages, and custom properties. These features facilitate the creation of targeted email campaigns that reflect where a contact is in their buying journey.

Dig deeper: From campaigns to conversations: The future of email marketing
Creating remarkable customer experiences

Meeting (and exceeding) customer expectations is not just about making a sale. It’s about building long-term relationships, fostering brand loyalty, and turning customers into advocates for your business. It’s about understanding that the customer experience doesn’t end with a purchase; it’s an ongoing journey that requires continuous engagement and nurturing.
